fix_commit.message: Bug 1941876 - Fix handling of dynamic elements when swapping objects r=jandem
fix_commit.author: Jon Coppeard

findings.title: Use-After-Free due to incorrect buffer ownership during object swap
findings.message: The prepareForSwap function only copies dynamic element buffers when the buffer is inside the nursery (ChunkPtrIsInsideNursery), but fails to consider the case where a tenured object with a buffer marked as nursery-owned is swapped with a nursery object. When swapping a nursery object with a tenured object, the tenured object can end up with a pointer to a buffer that is marked as nursery-owned. During the next nursery collection, this buffer will be freed because the GC believes it belongs to the nursery, causing a use-after-free when the tenured object later accesses the freed buffer.

related_locations.description: Function declaration missing 'other' parameter needed to check if swapping between nursery and tenured objects

findings.suggestion: The condition should check if the objects being swapped are in different memory regions (nursery vs tenured), not just whether the current buffer is in the nursery. When swapping between nursery and tenured objects, the buffer must be copied and marked with the correct ownership kind to match the destination object. Additionally, the function needs to account for shifted elements when copying the buffer.

findings.title: Shifted elements not accounted for during element buffer copy
findings.message: When copying dynamic element buffers during object swap, the code uses memmove with 'elements' (which points to the shifted position) rather than the unshifted header. Additionally, when assigning the new elements pointer, it does not account for the number of shifted elements. This causes the copied buffer to have an incorrect header pointer, leading to memory corruption when the shifted elements are accessed.
findings.suggestion: When copying the element buffer, use getUnshiftedElementsHeader() as the source, and when setting elements_, account for the number of shifted elements to point to the correct location in the new buffer.

ground_truth.root_cause: The introduction of the buffer allocator for JSObject elements changed how dynamic element buffers are managed during object swaps. The new code only copies buffers when they are physically inside the nursery memory region, but fails to consider cases where a buffer is allocated via AllocBuffer with nursery ownership semantics. When swapping objects between nursery and tenured heaps, the buffer ownership metadata can become inconsistent with the object's heap location, causing the GC to incorrectly free the buffer. The secondary issue is that shifted elements (array elements that have been logically removed from the front) are not accounted for when copying the buffer.

must_cover.reason: Contains the vulnerable code path where dynamic element buffers are only copied when physically inside the nursery (ChunkPtrIsInsideNursery check on line 1038), but fails to check buffer allocator ownership metadata. This misses cases where a tenured object has a buffer marked as nursery-owned, causing the buffer to be incorrectly freed during GC.

Orchestrates the object swap operation by calling prepareForSwap for both objects (lines 1304, 1307, 1312, 1315) and then fixupAfterSwap. Understanding this flow is essential to see that when swapping a nursery object with a tenured object, the tenured object can end up with a buffer pointer that has nursery ownership semantics even though the buffer is not in nursery memory.

Restores object state after swap but only handles slots correctly (lines 1093-1094). Lines 1097-1100 handle dynamic elements but rely on prepareForSwap having correctly saved the buffer. If prepareForSwap didn't copy a nursery-allocated buffer, fixupAfterSwap won't correct the issue, allowing the dangling pointer to persist.

Shows how element buffers are handled during nursery collection. This function allocates new tenured buffers (lines 931-941) and copies elements. A reviewer must understand that the GC will free nursery-allocated buffers after this, which is why the buffer ownership metadata must be consistent with the actual allocation site.
